header: Health check-up schedules (an annexure of a circular, one month) go into the table public.health_checkup_schedule, so that a question such as "which department is ticket 228757 in for the January 2025 health check-up" is answered with the person AND the date. npx tsx --env-file=.env.local scripts/import-health-checkups.ts lists the circulars that look like health check-up schedules npx tsx --env-file=.env.local scripts/import-health-checkups.ts --ids 23,30,37 DRY RUN: reads the pages, checks every row against HR, writes a report. Nothing is written to the database. npx tsx --env-file=.env.local scripts/import-health-checkups.ts --ids 23,30,37 --apply REALLY stores the rows (replacing that circular's rows) Before the first --apply run src/lib/nl2sql/sql/08_health_checkups.sql once in the Supabase SQL editor. How I find the date of a row: it is printed ONCE, in the middle of a merged cell that spans a whole group of rows, and the cell's ruled lines say which rows it covers (src/lib/ingestion/schedule/). How I trust a row: its ticket and name are checked against the HR directory (nlq.employees). A row is verified, corrected (a misread ticket fixed by the one HR employee with that name and department) or unverified (kept, flagged, never shown as confirmed). --apply refuses a circular whose pages show a problem (rows without a date, a group of an odd size, dates out of order) unless you add --accept-warnings after looking at the report. --pages-dir <folder> test aid: read the pages from <folder>/<circular id>/*.png instead of downloading them --fresh read the pages again even if a saved reading exists (health-cache/) The pages are read by Gemini (a primary and a checker model: OCR_PRIMARY_MODEL / OCR_CHECK_MODEL).
